solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tactless and absurd claim I'd put on

indicators.note: absurd suggests the letters of these words are put into a ridiculous new order

explanation.surface: Someone tactlessly makes a ridiculous claim while putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undiplomatic means lacking tact or sensitivity in dealing with people, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Unexpected result, winning over group of people

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, winning
a set is a group of people, as in the smart set

explanation.surface: A surprise sporting result in which a team wins over its supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset in sport is a surprise outcome where the favourite loses.

clue.text: A rude song at sea — dicey!

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Singing a vulgar shanty aboard ship could be risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicey is informal for risky or hazardous, a synonym of dangerous.

clue.text: Surprisingly static — reprove part of economy

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of the following words turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly stagnant business area earns a rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: The private sector is the portion of a national economy run by businesses rather than the state.

clue.text: Drug work — I scoffed

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed is ATE

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to swallowing a drug at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic drug derived from opium, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Official publicity cars pursued by turncoat, we hear

indicators.note: pursued by puts the following piece after what comes before it

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is publicity
Minis are small British cars

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken aloud and the letters entered only sound like it

parts.note: a turncoat is a traitor

explanation.surface: A government official's promotional fleet is followed by a defector.
explanation.walkthrough: TRATOR is not a word but, said aloud, it sounds like TRAITOR, the turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrator is an official who manages the affairs of an organisation.

clue.text: Watering hole popular before noon

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A pub that is busy even before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering hole is informal for a place to drink, and an inn is a pub.

clue.text: To some extent ironic entreaty for place to meet

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sarcastic plea, in part, for somewhere to get together.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', but that word is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition; 'place to meet' alone means the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre is a hub or venue where people gather, such as a community centre.

clue.text: Offence, capital, here in Egypt

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
capital as an adjective means excellent, first-rate, which is A1, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A crime committed in the capital city of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts toward Cairo, but here it means excellent, giving A1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the peninsula and mountain in Egypt, so the clue's place reference points to it.

clue.text: Excellent one mile motorway in French southeast

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
M is used for motorway in British road names like the M1
EN is the French word for in
SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: A wonderful single mile of motorway in the southeast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense is informal slang for great or superb, as well as meaning huge.

clue.text: Secure draw

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fasten or bind something
second meaning: a game ending level

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sports report, 'secure draw' sounds like holding on for a result; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie is to fasten with a knot, and a tie is also a match with equal scores.

clue.text: A non-drinker, Dan, in hospital department, waiting on

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

indicators.note: in puts Dan inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
the name as written

explanation.surface: Dan, a teetotaller, waits on patients in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiting on' is read adjectivally: an attendant is someone in waiting on another.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant serves or looks after someone, which is what being in service to them means.

clue.text: Close to leading, so animated!

indicators.note: animated suggests lively movement, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An excited cry about nearly being in the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means next to or beside, a synonym for close to.

clue.text: American animal, sullen? Not right

indicators.note: Not here means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: morose means sullen and gloomy

explanation.surface: A North American beast with a grumpy look, but not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is a large deer of North America, so an example of an animal there.

clue.text: Race in sea the French try at last

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
LE is French for the

indicators.note: at last picks only the final letter of the word try

explanation.surface: A swimming race in the sea, with a French competitor trying at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a swimming race in which competitors use several different strokes.

clue.text: Made verbal contribution identifying part of wheel

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rod joining the hub to the rim

explanation.walkthrough: 'Identifying' is just a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoke is the past tense of speak, and also a radial bar in a bicycle wheel.

clue.text: Faction starts to collapse acrimoniously: punch-ups on regular basis to follow!

indicators.note: to follow says the second piece comes after the first
starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next two words
on a regular basis takes every second letter of punch-ups

explanation.surface: A political group falling apart bitterly, with fistfights breaking out regularly afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a group or bloc within a political party, a faction.

clue.text: Rapid rise transformed poor condition

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sudden climb that turned into a state of decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is the state of a building or thing that has fallen into neglect and decay.

clue.text: Performance of group, Irish, grand initially

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An Irish band's grand concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is an informal word for a live music show or engagement.

clue.text: Campaigner good about environment (first and second)

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: the bracket keeps only the opening two letters of environment, dropping the rest of the word

explanation.surface: An eco-activist is good on environmental matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green is a campaigner for ecological causes, or a member of a Green party.

clue.text: Flexible English carry on in charge

parts.note: to last is to carry on, continue

explanation.surface: An adaptable English person keeps on running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means stretchy or adaptable, a direct synonym of flexible.

clue.text: Drink event with reduced prices failing to start

indicators.note: failing to start means the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a sale is an event at which goods are sold cheaply

explanation.surface: A drinks promotion that never got going.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer, so an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Hackneyed, ultimately worn-out, ceremonial

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of worn-out

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial act

explanation.surface: A worn-out, clichéd ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn-out' looks like the definition, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite describes a remark or idea overused to the point of staleness.

clue.text: Theatre specialist, participant in yen, euro, surge once

indicators.note: a participant is part of something, so the answer is a part of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A specialist caught up in a currency surge.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre means operating theatre here, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosurgeon operates on the brain and nerves in an operating theatre.
